answer.summary: No maximum savings figure for Pension Credit entitlement can be established from the supplied evidence, and the bundle's own status is 'insufficient'. The nearest relevant captured rule is not an eligibility cap at all: DMG Vol 14 Ch 84 (84911) sets a deemed weekly income tariff of £1 for each £500 of capital over £10,000, plus any remaining part-£500. That is an income-assessment rule feeding the financial test, not a cut-off beyond which entitlement ceases. The whole benefit comprises Guarantee Credit and Savings Credit; entitlement (DMG 77031) turns on presence in GB, qualifying age, satisfying the conditions for GC or SC, household/mixed-age rules, a valid claim and NI provisions. Capital must first be classified, owned, valued and reduced by disregards (84002), and a partner's capital is aggregated (84921), before deemed income arises. Whether a person still qualifies therefore depends on total income (including deemed income) against the appropriate minimum guarantee and, separately, on Savings Credit conditions and additional amounts — none of which the supplied records close. Required evidence pages (e.g. 84/0128, 77/0014, 77/0033) are recorded as missing or ungoverned, unit boundaries are machine-detected and unresolved, and capture dates are not effective dates. No individual entitlement or award is decided here.

answer.summary: Unverified model knowledge; no sources were supplied, so nothing below is source-verified and none of it should be treated as current-law confirmation. In general terms, moving permanently into a care home is not itself a reason for Pension Credit to end, and self-funding does not trigger disentitlement. Pension Credit remains a means-tested benefit for people over the qualifying age; residence in a care home is not an exclusion in the way it is for some other provision. What typically changes are components rather than the whole benefit: housing-related elements for the former home generally cease once it is no longer the normal home (subject to temporary-absence and sale-disregard rules), the carer addition can fall away if caring stops, and the severe disability addition depends on continuing qualifying disability benefit and on nobody being paid a carer's benefit. Self-funders usually keep Attendance Allowance or PIP daily living, because the 28-day suspension rule applies to publicly funded care, so a severe disability addition may continue where its own conditions are met. Capital is highly relevant: Pension Credit has no upper capital limit but deemed income above the capital disregard can reduce or extinguish entitlement, and the former home's value may be disregarded only for a limited period. Couples permanently separated by the move are normally assessed separately. Individual entitlement is not determined here.

answer.summary: Not established on this evidence. The supplied frozen DMG extracts do not contain any rule that State Pension Credit (SPC) ceases because a person moves permanently into a care home, whether self-funding or not; the evidence bundle is marked insufficient and most required records (including the care-home requirement profiles staff-012/staff-013 and the Pension Credit foundation profile) are missing. What the supplied extracts do show is narrower and component-level: (a) the general entitlement gates for SPC (DMG 77031) are unchanged by care-home status in the text supplied; (b) permanent care-home residents are normally resident in the home (DMG 78087) and the severe-disability additional amount can still apply under the heading covering self-funders, provided all its conditions are met (DMG 78088); (c) a member of a couple permanently in a care home is no longer in the same household as their partner, and each may claim as a claimant with no partner (DMG 78089; cf. DMG 77128); (d) the housing-costs additional amount should not be allowed for claimants in a care home unless absence from the home is temporary (DMG 78270). So the supplied evidence points to changes in additional amounts and household treatment, not to the whole benefit stopping. Self-funding status alone is not shown to determine any of this. Specialist review, legal-version reconciliation and individual facts remain outstanding; no entitlement decision is made here.
